submissions.title: IREN Delivers Horizon 1 to Microsoft and Achieves NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud Status on GB300 NVL72
submissions.excerpt: first 50MW (IT load) direct-to-chip liquid cooled AI Cloud deployment
submissions.note: First confirmed IT-load capacity at Childress: Horizon 1 (50MW IT load) delivered to and accepted by Microsoft under the $9.7B/5-year cloud contract (announced Nov 2025). Project record currently shows only a 750MW estimate with no confirmedMw. IREN is targeting 480MW gross AI Cloud capacity by end of 2026 and 1.2GW in 2027 (Horizons 2-4 still to come).

claims.methodology: Stated directly in IREN press release as IT load capacity of the delivered/accepted Horizon 1 deployment

submissions.title: TeraWulf Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results
submissions.excerpt: completed delivery of CB-3 in early July, increasing revenue-generating capacity to 102 MW
submissions.note: Lake Mariner reached 102MW revenue-generating critical IT capacity after CB-3 delivery (up from 81MW as of June 30, 2026), satisfying the condition for Google's $600M credit support backing Fluidstack's lease obligations to become effective. First confirmed MW figure for this project (record currently shows 360MW estimate only, no confirmedMw). IT-load/revenue-generating basis, not site power.

claims.methodology: Stated directly in TeraWulf Q2 2026 earnings release as revenue-generating critical IT capacity at Lake Mariner

submissions.title: TeraWulf Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results
submissions.excerpt: sell the Company's entire 50.1% interest in the Abernathy Joint Venture for aggregate cash consideration of approximately $530 million
submissions.note: Ownership change on a tracked UNDER_CONSTRUCTION project: TeraWulf agreed to sell its full 50.1% stake in the Abernathy JV to Fluidstack for ~$530M cash, making Fluidstack the sole owner. This is divestiture proceeds, not project capex or a power/compute figure -- flagging for the ownership/operator field rather than a capex claim.

submissions.title: NVIDIA Guarantees SB Energy's PORTS-Pike Technology Campus in Ohio to Exclusively Host NVIDIA AI Compute
submissions.excerpt: guarantee up to $105 billion in conditional lease and power payment obligations to SB Energy
submissions.suggestedProjectName: SB Energy PORTS-Pike Technology Campus (OpenAI/Nvidia, Pike County OH)
submissions.note: New, not-yet-tracked project: 8GW AI campus in Pike County, Ohio, developed/owned by SB Energy under a 20-year lease to OpenAI; Nvidia is the exclusive compute provider and separately invested $1.5B in SB Energy. Also disclosed via Nvidia SEC 8-K filing same week. Distinct from the already-tracked Stargate Lordstown, Ohio project (Related Digital/Oracle, Trumbull County -- different site and operator). Compute expected to start coming online in 2028; the $105B figure is a financing guarantee (lease + power payment backstop), not confirmed capex -- do not record as capex.

claims.methodology: 8GW dedicated AI computing capacity stated directly in the Nvidia/SB Energy joint announcement

submissions.title: Zerra DC files plans for large data center campus in Queensland, Australia
submissions.excerpt: proposing four 360MW data centre buildings delivered across four stages
submissions.suggestedProjectName: Zerra DC Western Downs Digital Park
submissions.note: New, not-yet-tracked project: development application (filed, not yet approved) for a 1.44GW, four-building AI campus near Dalby, Western Downs, Queensland. Singapore-based Zerra DC estimates AU$31B (~US$22.2B) at full build-out. Site power basis (four 360MW buildings per filing); pre-construction stage, no regulatory approval yet.

claims.methodology: Sum of four 360MW buildings stated in the development application as reported by DCD; not yet confirmed by regulatory approval
Developer's full-build-out estimate of AU$31B converted to USD as reported by DCD; unconfirmed against a filing

submissions.title: TVA to charge data centers more for power under separate rate
submissions.excerpt: new or expanding data center loads above 5 megawatts fall under a Capacity Commitment Charge
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: TVA's Board approved a new wholesale data-center rate class effective Oct 1, 2026. New/expanding data center loads above 5MW face a Capacity Commitment Charge (reported at roughly $1.5M/MW, paid over 3-5 years); existing data-center customers are moved out of the manufacturing rate class, raising their bills roughly 10% phased over 3 fiscal years. This is a utility connection/tariff rule change, not tied to one project -- relevant to any tracked project served by TVA (TN and adjoining parts of MS/AL/GA/KY/VA/NC).
